# Results — Study 877 (GDPNow Revisions)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: the Atlanta
Fed **GDPNow** nowcast is revised almost daily as data arrives, so the **revision** (the
day-over-day change in the current-quarter nowcast) is a real-time growth surprise that should
predict **next-day / next-week SPY** returns — and large downward revisions should precede
weakness. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; later forecast dates,
which have no complete forward SPY window, are dropped; the sample is pinned as-of 2026-06-30).
Fingerprint `6161199ecd72` (nowcast + revision + 1-day forward return).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real nowcast | Atlanta Fed **GDPNow** top-line real-GDP nowcast, daily forecast history from the public workbook `GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx` (`TrackingDeepArchives` 2011–2014 + `TrackingArchives` 2014–), **2,102** dated forecasts over **60** quarters, 2011-08-25 → 2026-06-26 |
| Signal | the **within-quarter day-over-day revision** of the nowcast (`groupby(quarter).diff()`, annualised-% points). The first forecast of each quarter has no revision and is dropped — **2,042** genuine revisions align to a complete forward SPY window |
| Return side | SPY daily **total-return** close (yfinance, `auto_adjust=True`), 2011 → 2026-06-30 |
| Execution / lag | one documented lag: the nowcast is posted intraday, so the **headline acts at the close of the release day** (lag 0). A stricter next-day lag (lag 1) is reported as robustness — and the sign does not survive it |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, Bartlett, 5-lag) *t* on the OLS slope and on each decile mean; Welch *t* on up-minus-down; a 5,000-draw permutation placebo; a two-era cut (split 2019-01-01); a 20-seed synthetic positive control |
| FRED note | FRED's CSV endpoint is firewalled in this build (as in siblings 385 / 268); the nowcast history comes straight from the Atlanta Fed workbook. FRED `GDPNOW` is the documented fallback in `data.fetch_nowcast`. |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** There is none to speak of: GDPNow is a single
public model series and SPY is a single index proxy, so no cross-section is curated. The honest
caveat here is **revision timing** — GDPNow updates post intraday after each release, so the
lag-0 headline is the *most generous* read (it lets you trade the release-day close); the
stricter next-day lag is weaker still.

## The headline — predictive regression of forward SPY on the revision

OLS `fwd_return = a + b · revision`, Newey-West(5) *t* on the slope `b` (n = **2,042**):

| horizon | slope `b` | NW *t* | *R²* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **1-day forward** (headline) | **−3.22 bps per 1pp** | **−1.02** | **0.043%** |
| 5-day forward | +1.47 bps per 1pp | +0.15 | 0.002% |
| 1-day, next-day lag (lag 1) | +3.27 bps per 1pp | +0.89 | 0.045% |
| 5-day, next-day lag (lag 1) | −3.08 bps per 1pp | −0.36 | 0.009% |

The revision **does not predict** the forward SPY return. The slope is insignificant at every
horizon (`|t| ≤ 1.02`), the *R²* is a **rounding error** (≤ 0.05%), and — the tell — the sign
**flips** the moment you move from trading the release-day close (lag 0) to the next day (lag
1). A real growth-surprise signal would not depend on being able to trade the same close on
which the nowcast is posted.

## Decile conditional — do the biggest up / down revisions move stocks?

Mean forward 1-day SPY return after the top-decile (biggest **up**) and bottom-decile (biggest
**down**) revisions; base forward 1-day return = **+5.56 bps** (n = 2,042):

| bucket | threshold | n | forward 1-day | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| top-decile **up**-revision | rev ≥ +0.300 pp | 205 | **−18.71 bps** | **−2.74** |
| bottom-decile **down**-revision | rev ≤ −0.350 pp | 205 | +0.09 bps | +0.01 |
| up − down (Welch *t*) | | | | **−1.64** |

This is the **opposite** of the claim on both counts. The claim says up-revisions predict
*strength* and down-revisions precede *weakness*. Instead the biggest **up**-revisions are
followed by next-day **weakness** (−18.71 bps, *t* = −2.74 — a "sell the good news" tell),
while the biggest **down**-revisions are dead **flat** (+0.09 bps, *t* = +0.01: the
downward-revision claim simply fails). And even that one significant number is **fragile**:
under the stricter next-day lag the top-decile bucket **flips to +11.24 bps (*t* = +1.33)** — an
intraday-reaction artefact of trading the release-day close, not a forecastable edge. A
significant **wrong-sign, lag-fragile** result is **None**, not a signal.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2019-01-01)

| era | slope `b` | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2011-01 → 2019-01 (n = 918) | +1.99 bps | **+0.19** |
| 2019-01 → 2026-06 (n = 1,124) | −3.57 bps | **−1.08** |

The already-insignificant slope **changes sign** across the two halves — there is no stable
relationship to speak of, in either direction.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) slope a lucky alignment?

Shuffle the forward returns against the revisions (breaking any link), 5,000 draws:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed slope | −3.22 bps |
| shuffled slope sd | 3.50 bps |
| two-sided *p* | **0.316** |

The observed slope sits comfortably inside the shuffled null — indistinguishable from noise.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Long SPY for one day after an up-revision (`rev > 0`), flat otherwise; one-way cost per turn:

| one-way cost | net/day | ann. | Sharpe (net) | vs buy-and-hold Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +0.36 bps | +0.9%/yr | **+0.07** | 0.80 |
| **5 bps** | −1.68 bps | −4.2%/yr | **−0.34** | 0.80 |

The rule is in the market only 48% of the time and earns a Sharpe of **0.07** at a generous 1 bp
one-way cost — a tenth of the **0.80** buy-and-hold delivers on the same dates — and goes
**negative** at 5 bps. Sitting out the market waiting for up-revisions forfeits far more drift
than the revision timing recovers. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded revision + forward-return frame with a tunable planted edge (up-revision
lifts the next-day return). No network.

| world | slope NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.18** (sd 1.01), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.005`, seed 877) | **+6.65** (beta +41.1 bps, *R²* 2.14%) |

The regression recovers a *planted* revision→return edge cleanly and never fires on the null —
so the flat real-tape result is a genuine absence of signal, not a broken test. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The GDPNow revision does **not** predict forward SPY with the claimed
  sign. The predictive slope is insignificant (1-day NW *t* = **−1.02**, *R²* = **0.043%**),
  sign-flips under a one-day execution lag and across the two eras (*t* = +0.19 / −1.08), and
  sits inside a permutation placebo (*p* = 0.32). The only significant piece — the top-decile
  **up**-revisions preceding next-day **weakness** (−18.71 bps, *t* = −2.74) — is **wrong-signed
  versus the claim** *and* evaporates (flips to +11.24 bps) once you can't trade the release-day
  close. Large **down**-revisions are flat (*t* = +0.01), so the downward-revision claim fails
  outright. A clean 20-seed synthetic control confirms the machinery is unbiased.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** An up-revision timer earns Sharpe **0.07** at 1 bp (vs 0.80
  buy-and-hold) and turns **negative** at 5 bps — sitting out the market's drift costs far more
  than the revision times.
